reason: The passage (Exodus 1:15-22) depicts Hebrew midwives who fear God (Elohim) and deliberately disobey Pharaoh's command to kill Hebrew male infants, choosing instead to preserve them. Their fear of God motivates their obedience, and God rewards their faithfulness by blessing them with households. As representatives of the Hebrew people, the midwives are portrayed as choosing allegiance to God over allegiance to a foreign ruler, demonstrating a covenantal relationship with the Divine. The passage shows the Hebrew people prospering under God's favor ('and God dealt well with the midwives...the people multiplied and grew very strong').
